note: Re-judged 2026-11-20 by an independent agent after 51799ad534 (owner ruling 5c) and the annotation correction that follows it. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "Since the SPD-I is just a part of the SPD, if a packet that is looked up in the SPD-I cannot be matched to an entry there, then the packet MUST be discarded." Producers read at HEAD: applyConfig now calls assertUnmatched, which on a reload runs installUnmatched and refuses the apply on any refused catch-all entry, and at start runs installUnmatchedAtStart, which keeps every accepted entry, refuses only a missing dataplane, logs the rest at Error under doctor-ipsec-spd-catch-all-missing and records it for the ipsec-spd-install check; placeXFRMInterfaceEntries and recordInterfaceCatchAllAtStart do the same for a bound XFRM interface's final entry, whose if_id 0 exemptions stay out. So a start whose catch-all was refused leaves a direction where an unmatched inbound packet meets no SPD-I entry and is delivered, a third path beside VPP (CatchAllSupported answers ErrNoNodeWideSPD) and the OSPF RFC 4552 manual-key entries. The corrected annotation names all three and the tests that show each (TestUnmatchedInstallFailureAtStartIsReportedByDoctor, TestInterfaceSPDCatchAllInstallFailureAtStartIsReportedByDoctor, TestUnmatchedInstallFailureFailsTheReload, TestUnmatchedWithNoDataplaneRefusesTheStart); every symbol it cites exists at HEAD. The gap stands.
